Now, two hundred years later, they had not only fully recovered from the devastation wrought by the Immortal Clans but had even flourished, rising to become an elite sect.
A certain piece of information about a groundbreaking discovery also began spreading like wildfire, sending shockwaves throughout the cultivation world.
The rumor was said to have originated from the Holy Continent, claiming that someone had discovered an entirely new type of spiritual energy—one even stronger than Immortal Qi.
It had first surfaced as nothing more than a whisper three hundred years ago, but now, it had grown into something far more substantial than a mere rumor.
"Have you heard?
They've named this new spiritual energy 'Celestial Qi,' and rumors claim that cultivating it could elevate an Immortal cultivator to godhood."
Kulas shared the news during a private meeting with Tian Yang and Ren Xia.
"Celestial Qi, huh?" Tian Yang muttered with a pondering look on his face.
"How was it even discovered in the first place?" Ren Xia asked.
"And has this person already gone past the True Immortal realm, which is said to be the limit right now?
Most importantly, can we trust this information?
There have been numerous frauds throughout the years, after all."
"I'm not sure how it was discovered, but the information is definitely trustworthy, as it came directly from the Three Pillars of Heaven."
"The pioneers of cultivation, huh?
If so, this is indeed massive," Tian Yang remarked.
"Maybe for them, but I highly doubt it will benefit us anytime soon," Ren Xia shrugged.
"The Three Pillars of Heaven will likely keep the method to cultivate Celestial Qi to themselves until they're far ahead of everyone else.
It's exactly what happened when they discovered Immortal Qi, too."
"What?
They discovered Immortal Qi as well?
How...?" Tian Yang muttered, stunned.
It almost felt as though the Three Pillars of Heaven were advancing the entire cultivation world on their own.
"They claim it came through enlightenment," Kulas said.

After a brief silence, he continued, "I only learned this because I once snuck into my father's room back when I was still in the Immortal Might Clan, but within the Three Pillars of Heaven, there is someone known as the 'Enlightened One'.

This person possesses a unique talent—the ability to receive divinations directly from Heaven itself through enlightenment, and it is through these enlightenments that they learned about cultivation."
"Seriously?
Divination from the Heavens?
That sounds like complete nonsense," Ren Xia scoffed, shaking her head.
"They're clearly hiding the truth behind some fancy story."
Kulas shrugged.
"Honestly?
As absurd as it sounds, I kind of believe it.
How else would they have discovered so much?"
"What do you think?" Both of them turned to Tian Yang.
"It does sound like nonsense at first," he admitted.
"However, I've witnessed things far more unbelievable, so it doesn't sound entirely impossible to me."
"Really?
Like what?" Ren Xia asked with a weird face.
He shook his head, his tone apologetic.
"It concerns the forbidden information within Han Zexian's tomb, so I cannot speak of it..."
"Oh?
More unbelievable than the Enlightened One?" Kulas replied with a smile.
"Now I'm really curious."

chapters.title: Chapter 2284 The Discovery of Celestial Qi
paragraphs: Although the discovery of Celestial Qi had shaken the cultivation world and dominated every conversation for a time, the excitement gradually waned. People began to realize that it might still take thousands of years before anyone outside the Three Pillars of Heaven could reach whatever lay beyond the Immortal Realm.

Time marched on, and more than a thousand years had passed since the discovery of Celestial Qi was first announced. With no further developments or reports, the world gradually lost interest to the point where many had forgotten it entirely.

Moreover, there were still very few cultivators who had even stepped into the Immortal Realm at this point, so for the vast majority of cultivators, the realm beyond it was something far beyond their dreams.

As for those in the Immortal Realm, they spent most of their time attempting to sense Celestial Qi. But without even knowing what they were searching for, the effort was no different from chasing a ghost.

During these thousand years, Tian Yang and Ren Xia remained on Giant's Continent. Tian Yang, although still stuck in the True Immortal realm, has qualified to become a level 6 Array Master, finally reaching Lu An's level. Kulas continued honing his combat experience through constant sparring with Tian Yang, and once he reached a level he deemed satisfactory, he shifted his focus entirely to developing the Giant's Continent and expanding the Giant Race's influence beyond its borders.
After a thousand years, Kulas' influence has surpassed even the Immortal Clans during their peak and has begun attracting the attention of other powerhouses, such as the Three Pillars of Heaven.

Meanwhile, Ren Xia caught up with their cultivation by reaching the True Immortal realm. Afterward, she took a break from alchemy to devote herself entirely to cultivation, harboring the faint hope of becoming the first to sense Celestial Qi and ascend beyond the Immortal Realm.
Of course, she knew the ambition was foolish—especially given how late she'd reached True Immortal—but she still wanted to try.

However, a few more thousand years passed with no progress related to Celestial Qi. By now, even Immortal cultivators had given up entirely, convinced that Celestial Qi had been nothing more than a hoax. And while the main cultivation world was bottlenecked, the rest of the world continued to advance swiftly, with new formations and pill recipes appearing almost every week.

"It's been five thousand years since the discovery of Celestial Qi, and the Three Pillars of Heaven haven't said a single word about it since. Are we sure they're not just playing us?" Ren Xia asked. She had long since lost most of her hope and couldn't help feeling skeptical.

"It's been five thousand years since the discovery of Celestial Qi, and the Three Pillars of Heaven haven't said a single word about it since. Are we sure they're not just playing us?" Ren Xia asked. She had long since lost most of her hope and couldn't help feeling skeptical.
"I cannot imagine why they would fabricate such a lie," Kulas replied, still placing faith in them. "Doing so would destroy their reputation, and their credibility would plummet to rock bottom.

He went on, "Be patient. Five thousand years is insignificant to cultivators like us. Each realm takes longer to advance than the last. Frankly, it wouldn't surprise me if no one breaks through to the next realm for another fifty thousand years, much less just five."
A few more years later, Tian Yang started to create his own world.
"Before you even create your world, you must decide where you want to put it," Lu An said to him.
"Where I want to put it, huh?" Tian Yang pondered for some time but couldn't think of anything.
"You got any suggestions?" He turned to ask Ren Xia.
"Can't we just put it somewhere around here?" she casually replied.

However, Lu An shook his head. "Since there's already a personal world within the palace, it would be wiser to establish yours elsewhere. Creating two worlds in close proximity carries unnecessary risks."
"Oh? What kind of danger are we talking about?" Tian Yang asked.

"To be frank, we aren't certain," Lu An replied. "It's purely conjecture for now, but caution is preferable to regret, especially considering how expensive creating worlds is. Nobody wants to waste their resources, after all."
"Makes sense, but what if we accidentally choose a location that's already near another world without realizing it?"
In response to Tian Yang's hypothetical question, Lu An could only offer a silent shrug.
"So, what do you intend to do? Will you leave to create your world?" Kulas asked.
Tian Yang nodded. "I haven't stepped outside this continent in over five millennia. It's about time I got some exercise. Still, I plan to return once my world is established.
"Is that so..." Kulas muttered before looking at Ren Xia. "What about you?"
"Isn't it obvious that I am going to follow him?" she immediately replied.
"I suppose so," Kulas said with a smile. "Alright then—good luck. I'll keep your room ready for you, even if it takes a hundred years."
"A hundred years? I highly doubt it'll take that long," said Tian Yang. "That said, we might travel the world a little before returning."
"Take as long as you need. There's no need to rush."

A few days later, Tian Yang and Ren Xia left the Giant's Continent for the first time in over five thousand years. Together, they wandered the Divine Heavens in search of a suitable place to create their own world.

They assumed the search wouldn't take long, but it proved far more difficult than expected. Even after a decade, they still couldn't find a suitable location. However, they didn't give up. They continued wandering the world, and creating their own world gradually became a secondary priority.
Fifty years into their journey, a new rumor began to spread around the world, and it was related to Celestial Qi.

"Did you hear? The Three Pillars of Heaven claims that someone in their family has successfully sensed Celestial Qi for the first time after its initial discovery five thousand years ago!" "Does this mean we might soon learn what lies beyond the True Immortal realm?"

"Hard to say. A mortal may sense spiritual energy, but that doesn't mean they can instantly draw it in and cultivate. They still require the appropriate technique. And even if the Three Pillars of Heaven already have the technique, it will still take time."
And just like that, Celestial Qi became a hot topic in the cultivation world again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2285 Sensing Celestial Qi
paragraphs: After seventy years had passed since Tian Yang and Ren Xia left Giant's Continent in search of a place to create their own world, they returned to the Giant's Continent as promised.
"Since you're back, it must mean that you've created your own world." Kulas greeted them with a wide smile.
"Where did you establish your world?" he then asked.
"Tha—"

"That's a secret just for the two of us," Ren Xia interrupted before Tian Yang could even fully open his mouth. Kulas shrugged lightly. "I don't particularly care where you choose to set up your love nest, but I must admit—I expected you to return with at least a child or two."
"What?" Ren Xia looked at him in disbelief.

"My family has tripled in size since your initial visit," Kulas continued. "And over the past seventy years, I have gained five more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, you don't have a single child even after five thousand years."

After a brief silence, Kulas asked with a solemn face, "Ren Xia... are you infertile?" Ren Xia trembled with anger at his outrageous assumption and snapped, "There is nothing wrong with me, and I am definitely not infertile! We don't have any children because neither of us cares to have one!"
Kulas blinked in surprise, then turned to Tian Yang. "For real? You don't want kids?"
Tian Yang silently nodded with a stiff smile.
Kulas turned back to Ren Xia. "And what about you? I find it hard to believe there are women out there who don't want children."
"What's so great about having children, anyway?" Ren Xia retorted. "Not only would we have to take care of them, but I'd also have to share my dear's love with them."
"Unbelievable..." Kulas muttered, looking utterly dumbfounded.
"Who are you to judge us?" Ren Xia shot back. "If anything, we should be judging you for having so many children. Do you even remember all their names?"
"Of course," Kulas replied with a confident nod. "Though... due to my position, I have to admit I don't exactly have the time to get to know them."
"I'm curious..." Tian Yang suddenly said. "What do you intend to do with so many children?"
"Well, someone has to inherit my throne one day—not to mention my legacy."
"And you need over three hundred children for that? You could do that with just one," Ren Xia retorted.

"That's true, but I'm an Emperor. What kind of Emperor has only a single child? And besides, there's no guarantee my first children will be qualified to inherit my legacy." Kulas said with a smile. "Anyway, let's put this topic behind us. Have you heard the Three Pillars of Heaven's latest announcement?"
"By latest, you mean what they claimed twenty years ago?" Tian Yang asked.
Kulas nodded, "That they have managed to sense Celestial Qi."
"What about it?"
"Truth is, I have also managed to sense Celestial Qi," Kulas revealed with a prideful smile.
"What?! Is that true?!" Ren Xia exclaimed.
Tian Yang then asked, "When did this happen?"
"Only a year ago," he revealed.
"Jealous? Want me to help you sense Celestial Qi?" Kulas teased.
"Can you really do that?" Tian Yang asked.
"I haven't tried it before, so I can't say for certain," Kulas admitted. "But it should be no different from helping a new cultivator sense spiritual energy for the first time."
"Then are you close to a breakthrough?" Ren Xia asked.
Kulas laughed.
"Of course not. Sensing Celestial Qi is one thing, but I still lack any real understanding of it. Forget cultivating it—I need to comprehend it first."
"Makes sense. So... any idea how long it'll take for you to figure it out?"
Kulas shrugged. "Not a clue. Honestly, I don't even know if I can comprehend it. It's hard to put into words, but once you sense it yourself, you'll get what I mean."
"For you to say something like that..." Tian Yang swallowed nervously. If even someone like Kulas lacked the confidence to comprehend Celestial Qi, then what chance did he have?
"Don't give up before you even start," said Kulas after noticing his expression. "Find me next week. I'll help you sense Celestial Qi first."
"Alright."
Tian Yang and Ren Xia returned to their old room shortly afterward. Just as Kulas had promised, he had kept the place spotless and free of dust for their return.

"To think we stayed here for five thousand years without a single advancement, yet the moment we leave, so many developments occur in such a short span... Is the world trying to tell us something?" Tian Yang wondered aloud as he reclined on the bed.
Ren Xia curled up beside him and let out a small laugh. "In that case... should we leave for another hundred years, then?"
"And do what?"
After a moment of silence, Ren Xia responded, "Dear... are you sure you don't want any children? If you're trying to be considerate..."
Tian Yang replied with a slight smile, "Are you asking me, or are you talking to yourself?"
She sighed. "Honestly, I'm not so sure anymore. Is it really that strange for a woman not to want children?"
"Then take all the time you need to think it over," Tian Yang said softly. "I'm certain I don't want any, but if you truly do, I wouldn't mind having one with you."
"If you say so..."
A week later, Tian Yang went to find Kulas.
"Anything I should know before we begin?" Tian Yang asked as he sat on the ground of the throne room.
"I don't think so."
"Then let's begin."
Kulas seated himself behind Tian Yang and placed his palms on his back.
"I will now attempt to sense Celestial Qi while sharing my senses with you. Whether you can also sense it will be entirely up to you," Kulas said as he closed his eyes.
"Whenever you're ready."
"I'm ready." Tian Yang said.
The very next moment, Kulas took a deep breath and began sharing his senses with Tian Yang.

chapters.title: Chapter 2286 Sensing Celestial Qi(2)
paragraphs: Once he confirmed that his senses were properly linked with Tian Yang's, Kulas began attempting to sense Celestial Qi.

However, even though he had managed to sense it before, it wasn't something he could replicate immediately. When he first successfully sensed Celestial Qi, it took him nearly ten years of straight cultivation.
Fortunately, he has gotten a lot better these days, and the last time it only took him a month.

Days passed in the blink of an eye, yet Tian Yang still couldn't sense anything different. Kulas hadn't sensed it either, of course, but Tian Yang didn't know that—and speaking might disrupt their concentration. So he stayed silent.
A little over a month later, Kulas finally began to sense the Celestial Qi around them. However, he stayed silent, allowing Tian Yang the chance to perceive it on his own.

Tian Yang, not knowing when—or if—he would sense anything, maintained his focus throughout the entire month. He could tell that something had changed through Kulas's senses, yet he still couldn't grasp it clearly himself.
'This feels just like when I was inside Han Zexian's cavern...' Tian Yang thought to himself, recognizing a familiar sensation in the struggle to comprehend the unknown.
Naturally, this was nothing like attempting to comprehend the forbidden knowledge that devoured his longevity. Compared to that ordeal, his current situation was considerably more comfortable.
Minutes turned into hours, and hours into days. In the blink of an eye, another month had passed, yet Tian Yang still made no progress.
After yet another month, Kulas opened his eyes and said, "Alright, that's enough for me. I can only stay in this state for so long before I'm mentally exhausted."
Tian Yang opened his eyes as well and let out a defeated sigh. "I wasn't able to sense it. Or rather... I sensed something, yet couldn't grasp it at all. Sorry for wasting your time."

Kulas let out a hearty laugh. "Did you truly expect to sense Celestial Qi so quickly? I certainly didn't think you would succeed on the first attempt. You may excel in comprehension, but Celestial Qi is something else altogether. It will be an obstacle even you will struggle with."
"Also, while I may be helping you sense Celestial Qi, I am also improving my own comprehension, so it's not like I am wasting any time."
"How often will we do this?" Tian Yang then asked.
"If every session takes around three months, we can do it two times a year. Once a year is fine if you want to take it slower." "Let's do it twice a year then."
"Very well."
Although he would only attempt to sense Celestial Qi with Kulas's assistance twice a year, Tian Yang continued to practice on his own whenever he had the time.
"Any progress?" Ren Xia asked Tian Yang after he returned from his tenth attempt to sense Celestial Qi.
"Nope."
A hundred attempts later—
"Any progress?"
Tian Yang could only silently shake his head.
In the end, it took Tian Yang over one thousand attempts and 250 years to finally sense Celestial Qi, albeit only a glimpse.
"I can sense it! I can sense Celestial Qi!" Tian Yang exclaimed with excitement the moment he sensed it.
It had been a long time since he experienced such excitement, and it made him feel like a child again.
"Good, now this is where the true trial begins..." Kulas remarked with a smile.
"Right..." Tian Yang's excitement quickly died down after he remembered that it would take more than just sensing Celestial Qi to reach the next cultivation realm.
"How's your progress?" Tian Yang then asked.

"As slow as a snail," Kulas shook his head. While Tian Yang had at last succeeded in sensing Celestial Qi, Kulas had shown almost no improvement, and his progress was barely any different from what it had been 250 years earlier when Tian Yang first started.
"At this rate, we probably won't see what's beyond the Immortal Realm for several more thousand years," Kulas sighed.

"That's a generous estimate," said Tian Yang. "Not only do we need to fully comprehend it, but we also need the proper technique to cultivate it. I have a feeling that we won't see any real progress for at least tens of thousands of years."

Kulas replied, "It sucks, but what can we do about it? With that said, it's not like it's a race—at least not for me—so I will be taking things nice and slowly." Now that he's managed to sense Celestial Qi, Tian Yang decided to continue cultivating to make sure it wasn't a fluke.
A year later, Tian Yang returned to Ren Xia with the results.
"Seeing how it took you much longer to return this time, I guess you've finally managed to sense Celestial Qi." Ren Xia said, reading him like an open book.
He nodded, "Now that I can sense Celestial Qi, I can help you sense it, too." However, Ren Xia shook her head.
"Thanks for the offer, but I want to try sensing it myself."
"Why?" Tian Yang asked, genuinely puzzled.
"Because of my pride," she replied calmly.
"I still don't understand."

Ren Xia took a breath before elaborating, "Kulas managed to sense Celestial Qi on his own. I... don't want to lose to him, so I'm going to do it myself. Of course, I'm not belittling your achievement. This is just my own stubborn pride. Moreover, it's not like I have anything else to do."
"If that's what you really want to do." Tian Yang nodded. "If you ever change your mind, I'll be here."
Ren Xia chuckled and said, "Who knows? Maybe I will even surpass you."

He smiled and said, "If you can truly comprehend Celestial Qi by yourself, then that is only a given. Hell, if it weren't for the Heaven Defying Ascension Pill, you would've already surpassed me in cultivation."
"Then how about a wager?" Ren Xia suddenly said. "Let's bet on whether I can sense Celestial Qi within five thousand years."
"What are we betting on?" "If I win, you must listen to one of my demands. If I lose, I'll listen to one of yours," she said.
"That's it?" Tian Yang raised his eyebrows. "If there's something you want from me, you can just ask me, you know?"
"I know, but I cannot think of anything else."
"I guess..."
"Then I'm going to start now!" Ren Xia wasted no time and immediately started her cultivation session.
'I should probably set a goal for myself, too.' Tian Yang thought to himself as his gaze lingered on Ren Xia for a minute before he also started his own cultivation.

Now that he could sense Celestial Qi, Tian Yang found himself spending more and more time in cultivation. At his current cultivation level, time moved beyond recognition, especially when cultivating, and what he perceived as minutes often slipped into years without him noticing.
One thousand years... two thousand years... four thousand years passed in the blink of an eye.

Although so much time had passed, little had changed in the cultivation world. However, more and more cultivators were now reaching the True Immortal realm and had begun attempting to sense Celestial Qi.
Then, another seven hundred years passed.
"Dear! I've done it!"
Tian Yang was in the middle of cultivation when he suddenly heard Ren Xia's excited voice coming from the room beside his.
When he opened his eyes, he could see her standing outside his open room with an exhilarated smile on her face.
"I can sense Celestial Qi!" she declared with a proud smile. "Oh? How long has it been?" he asked.
"Four thousand seven hundred and fifty-two years!" she immediately answered.
"To be honest, I was close to giving up," she suddenly continued. "However, in the end, I had an enlightenment." "An enlightenment? How did it feel?" Tian Yang asked, his interest piqued.

Ren Xia closed her eyes to recall the feeling and replied, "It's hard to explain... one moment I couldn't sense anything, and the next, I could suddenly feel Celestial Qi as if it had always been there."
She paused for a moment before adding, "To be honest, it feels unreal. I can sense Celestial Qi, yet it doesn't feel like something I accomplished. It feels as though it was given to me."

"What are you talking about? It's definitely your own achievement. Or what? Are you saying that Heaven took pity on you and directly helped you? Like the Enlightened One from the Three Pillars of Heaven?"
"If you put it like that..." Ren Xia muttered with a stiff smile.
"Anyway, this means I won the bet."
"Bet?" Tian Yang wore a puzzled face.
"Don't tell me you forgot?"
Tian Yang's expression froze for a moment before he suddenly recalled the bet.
"Ah, I remember now. Sorry, I actually forgot about it," he said.
"So, what do you want me to do for you?"
"I'll let you know once I think of something," she replied quickly.
"You had almost five thousand years to think..."
"Nonsense," she shot back. "I was completely focused on my goal. I didn't have any room left to think about anything else."
"If you say so." "And you? How close are you to understanding Celestial Qi?" she then asked.
Tian Yang offered a faint, bitter smile. "There were moments when I thought I was close. But the deeper I delve, the clearer it becomes that I've only touched the surface."
"I see... What about Kulas?"
"Actually, I haven't seen or spoken to him in a while now," he admitted. "Then let's go see him now. I can't wait to gloat," Ren Xia chuckled.
"Alright." He nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 2287 Mood Swings
paragraphs: Shortly after Ren Xia emerged from her successful seclusion, she and Tian Yang went to find Kulas.
However, when they arrived at the throne room, they were met with an unfamiliar sight. The usually unobstructed entrance was now guarded by two figures standing watch outside.
"Guards? Did something happen?" Tian Yang wondered out loud as they approached the room.
They have been living at the palace for thousands of years at this point, but this is the first time they've seen guards outside the room.
When the guards noticed Tian Yang and Ren Xia, they immediately bowed and said, "We greet Senior Tian and Senior Ren."
"Hey, we're here to speak with Kulas. He's inside, right?"
The guards nodded, but they continued to say, "Yes, but we cannot let you inside without the Giant Emperor's approval."
"What kind of absurdity is this?" Ren Xia said sharply. "We've walked in and out of this place freely for thousands of years. What changed?"
The guard offered an apologetic smile. "I'm aware, but these are His Majesty's orders. He expressly commanded us to prevent the two of you from entering without his consent."
"He mentioned us directly...?"
Tian Yang had a bad feeling about their situation, and he quickly said, "Then can you let Kulas know that we're here?"
"Of course."
One of the guards retrieved a communication jade slip and spoke into it.
Moments later, the guard returned and relayed Kulas's response.
"His Majesty says he's currently occupied and will meet with you next month."
"Next month?" Tian Yang raised an eyebrow.
Though a month was nothing to cultivators at their level, it still felt strange. Kulas had never made them wait before and had always prioritized them, no matter how busy he was.
"Alright, we'll come back later."

However, Tian Yang didn't linger and quickly left with Ren Xia. "Something feels off," he remarked as they returned to their room. "And it's not just the situation with Kulas. The atmosphere in this place feels different.
"When was the last time you left this room?" Ren Xia asked him.
"About two hundred years ago, so a lot could've happened."
"So what? Are we just going to wait?" she then asked.
"It's only a month. However, I can talk to someone else."
"You mean Chao Shuying?" "Or Xie Mey."

The following day, they went to look for Chao Shuying. However, they soon learned that she was no longer staying in the palace, having moved instead to the newly established alchemy school on the Giant's Continent.
"I forgot they created a school for Alchemists five hundred years ago after the success of their school for Array Master," Tian Yang remarked.
Since these places were relatively small and operated more like ordinary schools, they were classified as such rather than as sects or other formal establishments.

These schools accepted anyone willing to learn, regardless of background. They were also free to attend, making them immensely popular, so much so that humans would travel across great distances just to study on the continent.

Over the years, the Giant's Continent continued to expand, growing several times its original size. Not only that, its influence had already spread beyond the continent, and it was no longer an obscure power known to only a few.
In recent times, the Giant Race had begun appearing outside their continent, albeit only within nearby regions. Though they continued to draw attention and disdain, it wasn't as intense as before.
Not wanting to disturb Chao Shuying, Tian Yang went to find Xie Mey instead.
He quickly found her at the training ground.
"Senior Tian! It's been a while!" Xie Mey greeted him with a bright smile.
He nodded. "Indeed, it has."
"What brings you here?" she asked, eyes gleaming. "Don't tell me you came to see me? If so, this would be the first time you're the one seeking me out."
It has always been Xie Mey who approached him in the past, never the other way around. "Yes. I have a few questions."
The smile on Xie Mey's face faded, and she asked, "Have you spoken to my father yet?"
Tian Yang shook his head.
"He's busy, so I won't be able to see him for another month."
"I see. So you're here to ask me about my father's situation."
"Did something happen to him?" Xie Mey scratched her head and sighed, "Something did happen, but it isn't for me to tell you. If you want to know, you will have to hear it from my father."
Tian Yang fell silent for a moment before asking with a slight frown, "Is it really that serious?"
"Honestly...? Not really."
Tian Yang was left dumbfounded. How could it not be serious when everything pointed to the opposite?
Seeing his reaction, Xie Mey shrugged.
"You'll know once you speak with my father."
Since it was only a month, Tian Yang decided to wait it out.
Time seemed to pass far more slowly than usual for him, but eventually the month came to an end, and he was finally granted an audience with Kulas.
Tian Yang and Ren Xia followed the guard, who informed them that Kulas was waiting. Upon entering the throne room, they found Kulas seated on his throne, a perplexed expression on his face.
"What's going on? Did something happen while we were in seclusion?" Tian Yang went straight to the point and asked.
Kulas didn't immediately respond.
After a long minute of silence, he eventually let out a deep sigh.
"Honestly, I am still contemplating whether I should even tell you since it's a little embarrassing." "Embarrassing?" Tian Yang raised his eyebrows, looking confused.
"Stop beating around the bush and tell us already," Ren Xia said, sounding annoyed.
Kulas sighed once more before nodding, a defeated look crossing his face.

"I've been experiencing random mood swings that I cannot control lately—mostly anger. I thought I had completely moved past my old scars, but it seems my mental instability is slowly returning," he revealed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2288 Mood Swings(2)
paragraphs: Kulas continued, his voice heavy. "Because of these mood swings, my family has started avoiding me. They try to hide it, of course—but it's obvious to me."
"Wait... mood swings? That's it?" Ren Xia said, staring at him in disbelief. "Are you certain this isn't simply stress?"

Kulas nodded and elaborated, "The mood swings came out of nowhere and have only been growing more frequent. Not only can I no longer control them, but I'm starting to lose awareness altogether. I don't even realize it's happening until it's already over. There's no way stress would cause this."

Tian Yang then said, "I agree that this doesn't resemble stress. However, that doesn't necessarily mean your mental instability has returned. You've been stable for thousands of years—why would you suddenly regress? Was there some kind of trigger?"
Kulas pondered his question for a moment before shaking his head.
"No, not that I can think of any."
"Then there must be another explanation."
"Have you seen a doctor yet?" Ren Xia asked.
"That was the first thing I did when it started happening. I saw several of them, too. However, they were unable to find anything wrong with me."

"If I'm not ill and it isn't stress, then there is only one explanation remaining—my mind," Kulas sighed. "Despite our strong physiques and resilient mental fortitude, cultivators are not immune to mental damage. In fact, we are often more susceptible to it."
"What about a heart demon?" Tian Yang asked. "It's one of the most common issues cultivators face. What if a part of your mind still believes you're trapped in the Immortal Clan's dungeon?"
"I don't possess any heart demons. I've already taken the Demonic Manifestation Pill, a medicine designed to forcibly expose them, and it produced no response."
"Anyway, regardless of the cause, the reality remains that I'm causing trouble for my family," Kulas said. "Thankfully, you haven't seen my mood swings yet, and I intend to keep it that way."
"How do you intend to do that? These mood swings are random, right? Are you only going to meet us after you've had one? And how bad are these mood swings?" Tian Yang bombarded him with questions.

"From what I've heard, the mood swings aren't severe," Kulas explained, "but they're... unsightly. As for how I plan to make sure you don't witness them—I don't know yet. I'll think of something. Until then, it's best we limit our interactions."
Tian Yang narrowed his eyes. "Are you saying that because you don't want to trouble us?
"Of course. What else would it be?"

"And yet, that's exactly what you're doing," Tian Yang replied calmly. "Avoiding us isn't a solution. Even if you believe it's unbecoming, distancing yourself won't fix anything. You're simply running from the problem when we should be addressing it together. What do you think sworn brothers are for?"
"That's..." Kulas was left speechless by his words.
Tian Yang continued a moment later, "If you get it, let us help you."
A warm smile appeared on Kulas' face.
"Thanks."
Some time later, Kulas asked.
"By the way, why did you want to see me?"
Ren Xia smiled and replied, "I wanted to gloat."
"About what?"
"That I have managed to sense Celestial Qi all by myself," she revealed with a prideful look on her face.
Kulas offered no reply, only staring at her in stunned silence, his eyes widened and his mouth slightly open.
After a moment of silence, he shifted his gaze to Tian Yang and asked, "Is she telling the truth? You didn't help her at all?"
Tian Yang nodded with a smile.
"Yes, she's telling the truth. I offered to help her, but she refused."
"And it took me less than five thousand years," she added. "Now watch me enter the next realm before either of you will!" "Let's not get ahead of ourselves," Kulas shook his head.
They continued chatting for a little longer before Kulas brought up a new topic.
"By the way, this may sound random, but I have been wanting to do this for a very long time."
After taking a deep breath, he continued, "I am going to host a tournament on this continent."
"A tournament?" Tian Yang raised his eyebrows at this news.
Kulas confirmed with a nod.

"The participants will only be allowed to use their physique and techniques limited to strengthening their bodies, so there will be no weapons or martial techniques allowed. I am going to call it... the Tournament of Strength!" "Why are you suddenly hosting a tournament?" Tian Yang asked, puzzled by his intentions.

"Although anybody can participate, the giants will likely dominate it since we inherently have a superior physique. As for the purpose... I want to showcase the power of giants to the rest of the world. Oh, I also want to see if there are any excellent warriors out there for my children." "When are you going to host it?" "I don't have an exact date, but I have already begun the preparations. Maybe around fifty years from now."
"I see... I'm looking forward to it."
"You're participating, right?" Kulas suddenly asked with expectant eyes.
"What? Me?" Tian Yang almost couldn't believe his ears. "You want me to participate in a tournament? With my cultivation?"
"You won't be using your cultivation, though."
"It doesn't change the fact that I'll likely be competing with people with far less experience."
Kulas chuckled and said, "You don't have to give me an answer right now. Just think about it for now. I'll ask you again once I have all of the details ready."

"Whatever." A year later, Kulas officially announced the Tournament of Strength. It instantly became a sensation across the Giant's Continent and even drew the attention of those beyond its borders, especially after word of the tournament's rewards spread.
The tournament was scheduled to take place in fifty years, but people were already heading to Giant's Continent mere days after it was announced.
In the years that followed, the Giant's Continent became more crowded with visitors than ever before, including unexpected visitors from the Holy Continent.

"I don't possess any heart demons.
I've already taken the Demonic Manifestation Pill, a medicine designed to forcibly expose them, and it produced no response."
"Anyway, regardless of the cause, the reality remains that I'm causing trouble for my family," Kulas said.
"Thankfully, you haven't seen my mood swings yet, and I intend to keep it that way."
"How do you intend to do that?
These mood swings are random, right?
Are you only going to meet us after you've had one?
And how bad are these mood swings?" Tian Yang bombarded him with questions.
"From what I've heard, the mood swings aren't severe," Kulas explained, "but they're... unsightly.
As for how I plan to make sure you don't witness them—I don't know yet.
I'll think of something.
Until then, it's best we limit our interactions."
Tian Yang narrowed his eyes.
"Are you saying that because you don't want to trouble us?
"Of course.
What else would it be?"
"And yet, that's exactly what you're doing," Tian Yang replied calmly.
"Avoiding us isn't a solution.
Even if you believe it's unbecoming, distancing yourself won't fix anything.
You're simply running from the problem when we should be addressing it together.
What do you think sworn brothers are for?"
"That's..." Kulas was left speechless by his words.
Tian Yang continued a moment later, "If you get it, let us help you."
A warm smile appeared on Kulas' face.
"Thanks."
Some time later, Kulas asked.
"By the way, why did you want to see me?"
Ren Xia smiled and replied, "I wanted to gloat."
"About what?"
"That I have managed to sense Celestial Qi all by myself," she revealed with a prideful look on her face.
Kulas offered no reply, only staring at her in stunned silence, his eyes widened and his mouth slightly open.
After a moment of silence, he shifted his gaze to Tian Yang and asked, "Is she telling the truth?
You didn't help her at all?"
Tian Yang nodded with a smile.
"Yes, she's telling the truth.
I offered to help her, but she refused."
"And it took me less than five thousand years," she added.
"Now watch me enter the next realm before either of you will!" "Let's not get ahead of ourselves," Kulas shook his head.
They continued chatting for a little longer before Kulas brought up a new topic.
"By the way, this may sound random, but I have been wanting to do this for a very long time."
After taking a deep breath, he continued, "I am going to host a tournament on this continent."
"A tournament?" Tian Yang raised his eyebrows at this news.
Kulas confirmed with a nod.
"The participants will only be allowed to use their physique and techniques limited to strengthening their bodies, so there will be no weapons or martial techniques allowed.
I am going to call it... the Tournament of Strength!" "Why are you suddenly hosting a tournament?" Tian Yang asked, puzzled by his intentions.
"Although anybody can participate, the giants will likely dominate it since we inherently have a superior physique.
As for the purpose...
I want to showcase the power of giants to the rest of the world.
Oh, I also want to see if there are any excellent warriors out there for my children." "When are you going to host it?" "I don't have an exact date, but I have already begun the preparations.
Maybe around fifty years from now."
"I see...
I'm looking forward to it."
"You're participating, right?" Kulas suddenly asked with expectant eyes.
"What?
Me?" Tian Yang almost couldn't believe his ears.
"You want me to participate in a tournament?
With my cultivation?"
"You won't be using your cultivation, though."
"It doesn't change the fact that I'll likely be competing with people with far less experience."
Kulas chuckled and said, "You don't have to give me an answer right now.
Just think about it for now.
I'll ask you again once I have all of the details ready."
"Whatever." A year later, Kulas officially announced the Tournament of Strength.
It instantly became a sensation across the Giant's Continent and even drew the attention of those beyond its borders, especially after word of the tournament's rewards spread.
The tournament was scheduled to take place in fifty years, but people were already heading to Giant's Continent mere days after it was announced.
In the years that followed, the Giant's Continent became more crowded with visitors than ever before, including unexpected visitors from the Holy Continent.

chapters.title: Chapter 2289 A Faint Presence
paragraphs: "Hey, brother, are you sure you don't want to participate in the Tournament of Strength?" Kulas asked Tian Yang as the tournament day drew closer.
"How many times do I have to decline before you get it?" Tian Yang sighed. "But don't you want to show off your skills to the world?"
"Why the hell would I care about something like that? And it's not like the world isn't aware of me already. Have you forgotten who brought the downfall of the Immortal Clans?"

Tian Yang's war against the Immortal Clans had once made his name infamous across the Divine Heavens. However, with thousands of years having passed, his name—though not forgotten—was rarely mentioned anymore.
"Also, I am technically a criminal, you know?" Tian Yang said with a slight smile.

Kulas laughed out loud and said, "Who'd dare hunt the man who pretty much single-handedly defeated the Immortal Clans? If anyone were to go after you, it'd be the Three Pillars of Heaven, but seeing how they've ignored you, you don't have to worry about such a thing." "..."
After a moment of silence, Tian Yang spoke, "Now that you mentioned it... Why didn't the Three Pillars of Heaven do anything? They basically allowed the Immortal Clans to fall."
If the Three Pillars of Heaven had intervened with his revenge, the Immortal Clans would've likely still been as powerful as before.

"The Three Pillars of Heaven are not babysitters, nor do they have any reason to help the Immortal Clans. While they may have been on friendly terms, it's not like they were actual friends with each other."

Kulas paused briefly before continuing, "Speaking of the Three Pillars of Heaven, I received some interesting information about them yesterday. It appears that some of their people will be present at the tournament."
Tian Yang raised his eyebrows at this news.
"The Three Pillars of Heaven will be participating in the tournament?" he asked with a dumbfounded face.
"No, they won't be participating. They will only be spectating."
"I doubt they'll only be here to spectate."
Kulas nodded, "I'm sure they have business with me, but we know too little about them to make any speculations.
"Anyway, if you're not going to participate, what are you going to do? Just spectate?"
Tian Yang nodded.
"What a pity. The champion of the tournament will get to fight me, too."
"You make it sound like we haven't fought each other thousands of times by now. And I'm sure you wouldn't want to lose before so many people in public."
Kulas chuckled, "Now that you've mentioned it, we haven't sparred in a few hundred years, and I still haven't beaten you yet."
"If you want to fight, we can do it after the tournament."
"Sounds good." Kulas nodded.
Tian Yang then said, "By the way, how have you been feeling lately? I haven't seen any mood swings since you mentioned it nearly fifty years ago."
"I'm actually confused myself. I'd have mood swings several times a year, but after I spoke to you, it hasn't happened once. If I had known it would be like this, I would've told you soon."
"Regardless, this is a good thing."
"Of course." Kulas agreed with a smile.

As time passed and the tournament day drew closer, more and more people flocked to the Giant's Continent. Cultivators of great power and members of influential families alike arrived in droves, all eager to witness the prowess of the Giant Race firsthand.
Although rumors circulated that members of the Three Pillars of Heaven might appear, no one knew their identities—or if they would truly show up—leaving the crowds to speculate.
"It's been a while since I left the palace, so I'm going to leave for a bit." Tian Yang said as he approached the door.
"Where are you going? I'll go with you." Ren Xia said.
However, Tian Yang shook his head and said, "Sorry, but I want to go alone. I have been wanting to visit this place ever since I returned to this continent, but I never found the courage to do so."
Ren Xia realized where Tian Yang wanted to go and calmly nodded, "Alright. I won't bother you then.
"Thanks."
After leaving the palace, Tian Yang made his way to the place where he had first met Kulas... and where he had lost Huang Xiao Li.

Yet the continent had changed beyond recognition, its land expanded many times over. It took him considerable time to find the location, and when he finally stood there, it bore no resemblance to his memories. Given the thousands of years that had passed, that was only natural.
After standing motionless for many hours, Tian Yang finally reached into his pocket and retrieved a spatial ring.
"If reincarnation is real... are you somewhere in this vast world right now, living a vastly different life? Are you living a happy life? Would I even be able to recognize you?" he muttered.
Some time later, he put away the spatial ring and began walking a certain path.
Eventually, he reached an empty stretch of land. Once the entrance to Han Zexian's Tomb, it was now utterly barren, with no sign that the tomb had ever existed.

According to what he'd heard from Ren Xia, the Immortal Clans had taken full control of Han Zexian's Tomb after he entered the cavern. However, they soon realized that the trials no longer functioned, reducing the tomb to nothing more than an empty world.

After he escaped from the tomb, the Immortal Clans were forced to abandon the tomb as well because it started to collapse on itself. 'Kulas told me that he'd tried to find Han Zexian's Tomb again but to no avail... hmm?'
Tian Yang's thoughts were abruptly interrupted when he sensed a faint presence approaching from behind.
He turned around, and his eyes widened in shock and disbelief. It was someone he recognized.
Not only did he recognize them, but despite the thousands of years that had passed, they hadn't changed in the slightest.
However, before Tian Yang could snap out of his daze, the individual spoke first, "Tian Yang...?"
"Elder... Sun?" he responded.

chapters.title: Chapter 2290 Reunion With Elder Sun
paragraphs: The person standing before Tian Yang was none other than Elder Sun, and she looked exactly as she had the last time he saw her thousands of years ago, almost as though she hadn't aged a single second.

Elder Sun was a beautiful young woman with short black hair that barely brushed her shoulders, clear amber-colored eyes, a slender physique, and a rather ordinary stature. She wasn't the kind of breathtaking beauty that drew instant attention, yet there was a subtle aura about her—one that made her seem more beautiful the longer one looked.
"Tian Yang...? Is that really you?" Elder Sun said softly, blinking as if she couldn't quite believe her eyes.

Unlike herself, Tian Yang had changed tremendously since the last time she'd seen him. He had grown taller, more mature, and, of course, more handsome. He was no longer the young man who had always worried her.
Yet despite his transformation, Elder Sun recognized him almost immediately.
"Elder Sun... so you were alive." Tian Yang spoke with a relieved smile on his face.
"Why would I be dead?" she frowned slightly.

"Didn't you hear about what happened to the Immortal Monastery?" Tian Yang asked quickly. "They were dragged into my conflict with the Immortal Clans. Thousands of disciples died, and when I couldn't find you, I assumed you were dead."
He paused, then asked, "Where have you been? Why weren't you at the sect?"
Elder Sun sighed and replied, "I left the sect long before that happened. As for where I went... I returned to my hometown."
Tian Yang narrowed his eyes slightly before asking, "Would that happen to be... the Holy Continent?"
Her eyes widened with surprise.
"How did you know?"
Her reaction confirmed Tian Yang's suspicions. Elder Sun was undeniably from the Sun Family of the Three Pillars of Heaven.
"I overheard you speaking with another elder. I forgot her name, but I always see the two of you together."
"You mean Elder Jing?
Tian Yang nodded.
"And if you're from the Holy Continent... Do you also belong to the Sun Family, one of the Three Pillars of Heaven?" he continued to ask.
Elder Sun didn't immediately respond.

After a moment of silence, a slight smile tugged on her lips, and she spoke, "To find out so much about me, even though I've never told you anything... You must've spent a lot of time investigating me. Do you have a crush on me or something?"
"Don't flatter yourself, Elder Sun. I merely placed pieces of a puzzle together after learning of them by chance."
Elder Sun frowned, clearly displeased with his response, and said, "You can stop calling me Elder Sun. I lost the qualifications when I left the sect."
"Then what should I call you? Now that I think about it, I don't even know your full name."
"My name is... Rouxi... Sun Rouxi—but I forbid you from using my given name."

"If I cannot call you Elder Sun or use your given name, what am I supposed to call you? Sister Sun? Senior Sister?" Tian Yang said with a smile. "Well, you were always more like an elder sister to me than anything."
"An elder sister?" she sneered. "I thought you no longer wanted anything to do with me. Or have you forgotten about what you said to me when we last met?"
Tian Yang's expression stiffened when she brought up his previous outburst—that he had already severed their relationship.
"That's..."
Tian Yang opened his mouth slightly, only to close it again.

After a brief silence, he lowered his body and bowed to her. "This may sound like an excuse, but I was overwhelmed by emotion back then and wasn't thinking clearly. I've regretted not being able to apologize to you ever since."
He paused, then said softly, "I'm sorry. Truly."

"Ahem." Sun Rouxi cleared her throat, covering her mouth with a fist as she tried to hide the faint smile tugging at her lips. "Well, you were young and stupid back then, so I am willing to forgive you."

Tian Yang raised an eyebrow and asked, "Speaking of age... how old are you, exactly? You haven't changed even slightly since I last saw you, and you're even at the True Immortal Realm now. No... You were probably already an Immortal back then and were merely suppressing your cultivation."

"It's rude to ask a woman her age," she said with a faint smile. "But if you're imagining me as some ancient monster, you're mistaken. I'm at most a hundred years older than you. At our level, that's hardly worth mentioning. And no—I wasn't suppressing my cultivation back then. What you saw was my real cultivation.
"So you've managed to reach True Immortal since then? That's quite impressive."

"Who do you think you're talking to? If a talentless brat like you can reach True Immortal in a few thousand years, why can't I? I am a member of the Three Pillars of Heaven, pioneers of cultivation, you know?" "Honestly, besides that they discovered cultivation, I don't know much, if anything, about the Three Pillars of Heaven. In fact, I didn't even know about their existence until recently."
"There isn't much to know," she said. "We're no different from other families—just a bit larger and more secluded."
"That... sounds like an understatement." "If you're that curious, why don't you come to the Holy Continent and see for yourself?" Sun Rouxi suddenly said.
"What?" Tian Yang looked at her with a surprised face. "But from what I've been told, the Holy Continent is a special place that most cannot enter."
"That's true, but I can give you permission."
"Is it really that simple?"
She nodded.
"Pretty much."
"I'll think about it after the tournament ends," Tian Yang then said.
"Speaking of the tournament... Are you also here to spectate the tournament?" she asked.
"Something like that. In fact, I have been living here for the last several thousand years."
"This place? Why?" She tilted her head slightly with a puzzled look, unable to comprehend his choice.
"My best friend is the Giant Emperor, and I don't have anywhere else to go," he said.

chapters.title: Chapter 2291 Sun Rouxi
paragraphs: "You're friends with the Giant Emperor? Best friends, at that?" Sun Rouxi wore a surprised look on her face after hearing this information.
Tian Yang nodded.
"We've known each other long before he became the Giant Emperor, though."
Sun Rouxi suddenly fell silent with a pondering expression.

A moment later, she spoke, "Since you're his friend, do you think you can speak to him for me—the Three Pillars of Heaven? Although we came to spectate the tournament, our main purpose here is to speak with the Giant Emperor."
Tian Yang shook his head and said, "That won't be necessary. He is already expecting the Three Pillars of Heaven to contact him. But if you don't mind me asking, what business do you have with him?"
However, Sun Rouxi shrugged before replying, "I don't know. I tagged along on my own will, so I am not part of the main group."
"The main group... how many from the Three Pillars of Heaven are here?" he asked.
"Six people, excluding me. Two from the Ji Family, two from the Sun Family, and two from the Tian Family."
"I see... by the way, this may be a weird question, but what's the Tian Family like?"
Although he claimed that he wasn't interested in his real background, Tian Yang couldn't help himself.

"The Tian Family...?" Sun Rouxi looked at him with raised eyebrows, seemingly suspicious of his intentions. After a moment of silence, she responded, "You'll need to be more specific than that. Just what do you want to know about them?"

"If it's not too much to ask... What kind of unique prowess do they possess?" "What?" Sun Rouxi narrowed her eyes. "Unique prowess... as in the power of their bloodline? Why do you want to know about something like that?"
"I heard a certain rumor and just wanted to confirm something."

"Is that so... Unfortunately, I cannot disclose such sensitive information, even if that person is you. In fact, I'll likely face the death sentence if I reveal such information to an outsider. If you really want to know, you'll have to visit the Tian Family and ask them yourself."
Tian Yang shook his head, "It's nothing more than blind curiosity."
"Anyway, I'll be returning to the palace soon. Want to meet the Giant Emperor now? You can speak with him yourself."
Sun Rouxi then said, "Actually, I only intended to visit this place briefly. Someone is waiting for my return, so I'll visit the palace afterward."
"Oh? Did you finally get yourself a partner after so long?" Tian Yang remarked with a smile.
She immediately frowned.
"What nonsense are you talking about? I came here with my friend, who you know as Elder Jing."
"Hm? Elder Jing? She also left the sect?"
"Yes, and she has been staying at the Sun Family with me."
"You're practically sisters now." "I guess so."
"Then visit the palace whenever you're ready. I'll see you then."
Tian Yang didn't linger and left the next moment, leaving Sun Rouxi behind.
She didn't immediately leave and stayed behind to watch his figure quickly disappear into the horizon.
"So you had been hiding here for the last several thousand years. No wonder I couldn't find you..." she mumbled in a low voice.
Some time later, she also left, returning to where Elder Jing was waiting.
"Hm? Back so soon already?" Elder Jing remarked when Sun Rouxi returned.
Elder Jing raised an eyebrow when she saw the look on Sun Rouxi's face.
"Did something happen? The last time you showed such a smile was when you learned that Disciple was alive."
Sun Rouxi chuckled, "You won't believe who I met just now."
"No way..." Elder Jing stood up with a dumbfounded look on her face. "Don't tell me..."
"Yes, I met him."
"Seriously...?"
Sun Rouxi continued, "The reason we couldn't track him after the Immortal Clans' downfall was because he'd been living quietly on this continent for the past several thousand years."

What she didn't mention to Tian Yang was that she had been keeping tabs on him all this time—much like how he had been watching over Kulas while he was still trying to conquer the continent. She was aware of nearly every move he'd made, right up until the moment he vanished without a trace.

"That's an overstatement," said Tian Yang.

"Your room...?" Sun Rouxi murmured with a somewhat dazed face.

Some time later.
"Then I'll be back."
After leaving Sun Rouxi in his room with Ren Xia, Tian Yang went to find Kulas.
"My husband speaks quite highly of you, Elder Sun." Ren Xia started a conversation not even a minute after Tian Yang left.
"Your husband...?" Sun Rouxi's eyebrows raised slightly at her words.

"Is that so..."
Ren Xia glared at Sun Rouxi, scrutinizing every subtle reaction she showed.
'Her reactions are weak... Not what I had anticipated at all...' Ren Xia thought to herself.

paragraphs: "You know, I have heard a lot about you from my husband," Ren Xia continued.
Sun Rouxi raised an eyebrow, her eyes flickering with intrigue. "Oh? What does he say about me?"
"He said you were always nagging at him." Ren Xia chuckled. "That you made his life in the Immortal Monastery more difficult than it had to be."
Sun Rouxi shook her head with a bittersweet smile and replied, "If I didn't nag at him, who would? He was always getting into trouble, acting recklessly and without a care for his life."
"So he was like that as a disciple, too, huh? I thought it was something he picked up after he left the sect." Ren Xia remarked with a surprised look on her face.

"It was a habit of his to belittle himself, calling himself talentless and whatnot. And because of his lack of talent, he would constantly push himself to the brink of death. I have lost count of how many times I had to save him."
Sun Rouxi glared at Ren Xia and asked, "What do you like about that brat, anyway? Aren't you a young lady of the Immortal Clans?"
Ren Xia chuckled and replied, "It's precisely his recklessness that I love."

She narrowed her eyes slightly and continued, "And you? What was it about him that made you keep an eye on him? Disciples getting into trouble happens all the time, yet you specifically decided to pay special attention to him."
Sun Rouxi lifted her head to stare at the empty ceiling. After a moment of silence, she muttered, "I wonder."
"What?" Ren Xia raised an eyebrow.

Sun Rouxi continued with a profound smile, "If you think about it, there's really nothing truly special about Tian Yang as a disciple. If you saw him in a crowd, he was just like any other disciple, completely ordinary. While his recklessness is on another level, he wasn't the only disciple desperate for improvement. I see them almost daily. However, there was just something about him that I couldn't ignore, and I am still trying to figure out the cause even to this day."
"That sounds like love at first sight," Ren Xia chuckled.
"What?" Sun Rouxi looked at her with wide eyes, almost as if she couldn't believe her ears.
She then spoke, "I may not understand why I was attracted to him, but I can say with certainty that it wasn't such emotions. I just got this feeling that I couldn't leave him alone."
"I was only joking." Ren Xia shook her head with a smile.

"If you don't mind me asking... Why was someone like you working as a sect elder at the Immortal Monastery? You're a member of the Three Pillars of Heaven, right? With your qualifications, you could even ask to be its sect leader, let alone a sect elder."
"Sorry, but I cannot tell you the reason. However, I can tell you that nobody at the sect was aware of my true background, as that would've defeated my purpose for being there in the first place."
'So she was in a situation where she had to keep her background hidden, huh?' Ren Xia thought to herself.
As someone from a privileged background, she could think of several reasons why Sun Rouxi had to conceal her identity.
While Ren Xia and Sun Rouxi continued their conversation, Tian Yang spoke with Kulas.
"So the Three Pillars of Heaven have business with me, huh? Well, I had already anticipated something like this when I heard they would show up."
"Do you mind speaking with one of them right now? She's..." Tian Yang explained the whole situation to Kulas.
"What? Elder Sun?" Kulas' eyes widened with surprise at the news. "To think you'd meet her by chance... this is more than mere coincidence. It must be fate."
"Alright, I'll meet with her," he agreed.
Tian Yang returned to tell Sun Rouxi of Kulas' approval and brought her to meet him.
Some time later...
"It's an honor to meet you, Giant Emperor." Sun Rouxi politely greeted him.
"You can drop the formality." Kulas casually waved dismissively. "You may not remember, but this is actually our second meeting."
"Oh? Where and when did we last meet?" Sun Rouxi asked.
"Here, on this continent. Right before the opening of Han Zexian's Tomb. Moments after you spoke with my dear friend."
"Then you're..." Sun Rouxi immediately recalled Kulas' words to her on that day.
Kulas silently nodded in confirmation.
"You should've seen his face afterward." Kulas laughed out loud. "It had nothing but guilt all over it."
Hearing such words, Sun Rouxi subconsciously shifted her gaze to Tian Yang, who was sighing as he rubbed his eyes.
"Anyway, why did you want to meet with me?"
"The Three Pillars of Heaven has something they would like to discuss with you, and I wanted to see if we could schedule a meeting."

"Schedule a meeting? You're more reserved than I expected. I was anticipating the Three Pillars of Heaven to simply walk in here and demand an audience like they own the place." Kulas remarked with a smile.
"To be honest, they'll likely do that if you refuse."
Kulas then said, "Since you're already here, why don't you tell me what the Three Pillars of Heaven want from me?"

Sun Rouxi shook her head and explained, "I may have come here with them, but I am not part of the discussion, so I don't know what business they have with you." "Is that so? Then, do you mind me asking what sort of position you stand within the Three Pillars of Heaven?"
"My position, huh? I am just one of many in the main family. It's nothing impressive."
Kulas could sense that Sun Rouxi wasn't giving the full details, but decided to ignore it because of her relationship with Tian Yang.
"Very well. If the Three Pillars of Heaven want to speak with me, we can do so after the Tournament of Strength. It's not like I can turn away the most powerful family in the world, anyway."
"Thank you."
"Since you're someone close to my brother, I'll let you linger at the palace as well. Just don't wander around alone."
"I understand."
After her audience with Kulas, Sun Rouxi stayed a little longer to chat with Tian Yang.
"Hey, why don't we have a little spar?" Sun Rouxi suddenly said.
"Out of nowhere?" Tian Yang looked at her with a weird expression.
"I want to see how much you've grown."
Tian Yang smiled and said, "Don't complain if you lose."
"Lose? To you? When have I ever lost to you? You may be a True Immortal now, but that won't change anything.
"If you say so."
Tian Yang brought her to the training ground inside Kulas' world.
"This is... a personal world?" Sun Rouxi seemed to be surprised by its existence. "You look surprised. Don't you have plenty of these at the Holy Continent?"
"What? Who told you that?" Sun Rouxi looked at him with a puzzled face.
"Nobody. It was just my own speculation."

"What a wild speculation. Do you think it's easy to create personal worlds? It requires a tremendous amount of resources and time. Even the Three Pillars of Heaven cannot make them willy-nilly. While we do have a few, they're all used as secret vaults, not as a training ground like this..."
"Anyway, for this spar, I won't use my family's techniques to make things fair," she then said.

However, Tian Yang shook his head and said, "Aren't you underestimating me a little too much? You're already going to lose, so why cripple yourself even more?" "Looks like you've gotten quite arrogant since the last time I saw you," she said. "How about this? If you can force me to use my family's martial techniques, I will owe you a favor."
"You know that I defeated the Immortal Clans, right?" Tian Yang said.
"Of course."
"Yet you're still underestimating me... You must be powerful enough to crush the Immortal Clans effortlessly, then."
Sun Rouxi quickly responded with a confident smile, "If I really wanted to? I could've dealt with them in a few days."
"Now I really cannot wait to fight you." Tian Yang said as he beckoned her. "I'm ready whenever you are."
"As your senior, I'll let you make the first move," she said.
"Then I won't be humble!" Tian Yang immediately made his move without hesitation, striking her with a lightning-quick sword technique.
In response, Sun Rouxi used a movement technique, easily avoiding his sword technique.
Tian Yang immediately followed up with another sword technique, one that Sun Rouxi was very familiar with.
"The Immortal Monastery's sword techniques?"
"There's more where that came from!" Tian Yang laughed as he continued using the Immortal Monastery's martial techniques.
"You kept training their techniques even after you left? Why?" she eventually asked. "I'm sure you have acquired many powerful and high-ranking techniques."
"I didn't practice them out of nostalgia or anything," he said with a smile. "For some reason, using them puts me at ease, so I do so from time to time—to clear my mind or as a warm-up."
"Seriously? This is the first time I've heard of such a thing."
"What about your techniques? If they're not from the Immortal Monastery or your family, where'd you learn such techniques?" Tian Yang asked her.
"There is something called the Heavenly Knowledge within the Three Pillars of Heaven. It contains countless nameless techniques created by the three families."
"What? Isn't that technically techniques from your family?"

"Technically, yes, but the ones I am using aren't created by my family but the other two families, so it's fine. Also, most of these techniques are either abandoned or unfinished, hence why they're nameless," she explained.

"I didn't practice them out of nostalgia or anything," he said with a smile.
"For some reason, using them puts me at ease, so I do so from time to time—to clear my mind or as a warm-up."
"Seriously?
This is the first time I've heard of such a thing."
"What about your techniques?
If they're not from the Immortal Monastery or your family, where'd you learn such techniques?" Tian Yang asked her.
"There is something called the Heavenly Knowledge within the Three Pillars of Heaven.
It contains countless nameless techniques created by the three families."
"What?
Isn't that technically techniques from your family?"
"Technically, yes, but the ones I am using aren't created by my family but the other two families, so it's fine.
Also, most of these techniques are either abandoned or unfinished, hence why they're nameless," she explained.

chapters.title: Chapter 2293 Tournament of Strength Begins
paragraphs: "Heavenly Knowledge? Such a name for a place to throw away unfinished techniques. Why'd you even learn them? And are you sure it's okay to tell me about such a place? Won't you be punished?" Tian Yang questioned.
Sun Rouxi shrugged, "The Heavenly Knowledge is not a secretive place. Anyone within the Three Pillars of Heaven can access it. As for why I learned them... It's a good way to practice."
"Practice?" Tian Yang asked, a puzzled expression on his face.
"Trying to comprehend and complete the unfinished techniques—turning them into your own," she replied calmly.

Although Sun Rouxi made it sound like an ordinary thing, it was anything but. Completing another person's unfinished technique required tremendous talent and experience, an achievement few cultivators could ever hope to accomplish.
"There is not much to do at the Three Pillars of Heaven, so I spent most of my time cultivating and finishing techniques."
"That's how you spent the last few thousand years?"
"It's a bit boring when compared to your little adventure, isn't it? Anyway, enough chitchat. Let's continue." Sun Rouxi went on the offensive this time.
Her movements were swift and graceful, like a dancer on a stage.
As their spar continued, Tian Yang noticed that he was starting to get pushed back by her.
'Even though I am not using any of my main techniques, to be pushing me back...'
Tian Yang was truly surprised that he wasn't able to overwhelm Sun Rouxi despite his vast experience.
'Even though I should have more experience than her... how is she this powerful? This is what true talent looks like?'
He finally understood that Sun Rouxi hadn't been looking down on him. However, that didn't mean he would give up.
"Hm? Looks like you're finally starting to fight seriously," Sun Rouxi remarked as she noticed a shift in Tian Yang's movements.
"Yes, looks like I had been the one underestimating you this entire time." Tian Yang said. "I'll be fighting seriously now, so... try not to get hurt!"
Tian Yang unleashed Limitless Sword Domain and started using other powerful martial techniques, instantly turning the tide.
'So this is the Immortal Slayer who caused the Immortal Clans' downfall...' Sun Rouxi smiled inwardly after experiencing the legend herself.
However, as much as she wanted to enjoy the moment, she knew that she could no longer take the spar lightly.

Thus, they started fighting seriously. While it wasn't at the level where they were trying to kill each other, they were fighting with the intent of defeating the other, even if it was a little dangerous.
A few hours later.
"You're really something, Tian Yang. Not even the geniuses at the Three Pillars of Heaven could push me this far," Sun Rouxi remarked, her entire body soaked in sweat.
"I could say the same... Not even Kulas could make me bleed this much..." Tian Yang said, his body soaked in sweat and blood.
'I must admit...' Sun Rouxi thought to herself. 'I won't be able to defeat him at this rate. However, if I lose my family's techniques... I might as well surrender.'
Meanwhile, Tian Yang pondered how he could force her to use the Sun Family's techniques.
Then, after a few thousand more exchanges, Sun Rouxi suddenly said, "Hah. I'm tired. I surrender."
"What? Surrendering before you are forced to use your family's technique? That's cheating."
Sun Rouxi smiled and said, "Since I admit defeat, even though I didn't use my family's techniques, I'll owe you a favor.
"Well, if you admit defeat..."
Although he won, Tian Yang wasn't happy. He knew that if Sun Rouxi started using her family's technique, he would definitely have lost.
"I still have a long way to go, huh?" he muttered.
"What?" Sun Rouxi, who heard his mumble, uttered. "You're plenty strong enough already. What are you going to do with more power? Are you going to challenge the Three Pillars of Heaven next?"

Tian Yang raised an eyebrow and replied, "Challenge the Three Pillars of Heaven? I may be reckless, but I am not suicidal. Also, why would I challenge them in the first place? It's not like we have any grudges."
"I guess so..."
Sun Rouxi fell silent, her gaze fixated on him.
"If you have something you want to say, just say it." Tian Yang said, noticing her odd gaze.
"Why... did you go after the Immortal Clans? Is it related to why your outburst on that day?" she asked with some hesitancy in her voice.
This was something she had always wanted to figure out. The reason for his hatred toward the Immortal Clans, and why he'd said such things to her.
"If you don't want to tell me, that's fine." After a moment of silence, Tian Yang shook his head and said, "No, you have the right to know after what happened."
"It might take a while, so why don't we do it somewhere more comfortable? I also want to wash up first."
"Okay."
They left the training ground and returned to Tian Yang's room.
After they both washed up, they sat down with some hot tea.
"I will tell you everything from the start."
Tian Yang said, and he started telling Sun Rouxi about everything that had occurred since he left the Immortal Monastery.
From his meeting with the Huang Family to how they survived a mythical beast because of her life-saving treasure, and what happened on the Desolate Continent that led him to Han Zexian's Tomb.
"I see..."

Ever since that incident, she had been trying to figure out the cause and what she had done wrong. Now, after thousands of years of doubt and confusion, Sun Rouxi finally learned the reason behind Tian Yang's anger on that day.
"If I were in your shoes, I would also be angry. However, I must correct you on something," she suddenly said.
"What?" Tian Yang looked at her with a puzzled face.

"That life-saving treasure... even if you had known about it in advance, you wouldn't have been able to save the whole family. After all, life-saving treasures are typically meant for a single person for maximum efficiency." "It was already a miracle that it managed to activate for two people. If you had tried to use it for the whole family, it would've likely picked its target at random, leaving behind the others or... not activate at all."
"Seriously...?" Tian Yang swallowed nervously at her words.
Sun Rouxi took out the life-saving treasure she'd retrieved from Tian Yang in the past and showed it to him.
"If you don't believe me, you can try it."
Tian Yang sighed, "There's no need. I believe you. It's just that... now I feel even more guilty for trying to blame you."
"No point dwelling in the past," she said before suddenly narrowing her eyes at him.
'But still... to think it was all because of another woman...'
Sun Rouxi felt a little annoyed for some reason.
Time continued to pass, and a few days later, the Tournament of Strength officially began.

The tournament was held on an artificial island near the Giant's Continent. Kulas had originally planned to host it within the city, but with thousands—no, hundreds of thousands—of participants registering, he made a last-minute decision to move it elsewhere.
"Wow, there are a lot more people here than I anticipated." Ren Xia remarked after seeing the crowd that had come to spectate.
"This just shows how much influence the Giant's Race now has," Kulas spoke with a satisfied smile.
He turned to look at Tian Yang and continued, "This is your last chance to participate." "Yeah, no thanks."
Kulas sucked his teeth but didn't pursue it any further.
"Where's Elder Sun?" Ren Xia then asked. "I thought she would be watching it with us."
"She's with her family," Tian Yang said. "Is that so..."

Some time later, Kulas left his area and entered the stage. Although he didn't make a single sound when he appeared on the stage, the loud audience instantly halted their movements and stopped talking after sensing the immense pressure he exuded.
"Welcome to the Giant's Continent. I am Giant Emperor Kulas, the ruler of this land."
After a brief introduction, he started listing the rules. Then, without any delay, immediately started the tournament.
Given the sheer number of participants, the majority of whom were human, the tournament was bound to span days—perhaps even weeks—even if the battles continued without pause.

Once the tournament began, multiple matches unfolded simultaneously. Kulas watched from his private viewing area, with Tian Yang and Ren Xia seated beside him—a privilege not even his own children enjoyed. This arrangement drew the attention of many onlookers, especially those from powerful backgrounds.
"Who are those two sitting beside the Giant Emperor? They look like humans. Could they be his children?"
"Doubtful. Look at that area below him. All of his children are there."
"Look at the Giant Emperor. He's laughing with them."

Unbeknownst to a few people, Tian Yang and Ren Xia were actually in disguise, so it was not surprising that nobody recognized them. However, even if they weren't disguised, it was unlikely that anybody would recognize them. Still, they didn't want any unnecessary attention, hence the disguise.
"That's Tian Yang? He looks so different from my memories." Elder Jing remarked after seeing Tian Yang again. "I thought he would be more handsome."
Sun Rouxi smiled and said, "He's in a disguise."
"Hm? Really? Why?"
"He did cause the Immortal Clans' downfall..."
"If the Three Pillars of Heaven aren't going after them, who else would?"
"Who knows? Better be safe than sorry."
